about: Zahra S. Karinshak is a partner at Krevolin & Horst, located in Atlanta, Georgia. Representing clients throughout the country, she focuses her practice on whistleblower cases (False Claims Act/qui tam), white collar criminal defense, civil rights, employment, and complex civil litigation (representing both plaintiffs and defendants). For 8 years, Zahra served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Georgia. As a military veteran and former state Senator, she has extensive experience dealing with the government for the benefit of her clients.

Zahra earned her Bachelor of Science from the United States Air Force Academy in 1989. Upon graduation, she served as an Intelligence Officer in the U.S. Air Force. Zahra subsequently attended Emory University School of Law, where she was awarded her Juris Doctor with distinction in 1997. Upon graduation, Zahra served as a law clerk on the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals for the Honorable J.L. Edmondson. Before joining Krevolin & Horst in 2011, Zahra spent eight years as an Assistant U.S. Attorney (prosecutor) in the United States Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Georgia. She also served as Deputy Counsel for the Governor of Georgia and as a litigator at Sutherland (now Eversheds Sutherland). Admitted to practice in Georgia, Zahra is also admitted to practice before the U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Georgia, the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

As a result of her zealous advocacy on behalf of her clients and her high ethical standards, Zahra has received recognition from her fellow professionals, including an AV Preeminent* peer review rating through Martindale-Hubbell and a "Superb" peer-review rating through Avvo. Dedicated to her profession and community, Zahra is a member of the Atlanta Bar Association, the Gwinnett Chamber of Commerce, the Georgia Association for Women Lawyers, the Georgia Asian Pacific American Bar Association, and numerous charitable organizations. She is a graduate of Leadership Gwinnett Class of 2014, Leadership Georgia Class of 2003, and serves on the Board of Governors for the Georgia State Bar.

*AV Preeminent and BV Distinguished are certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the confidential opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell ratings fall into two categories: legal ability and general ethical standards.
